### Close skips pending async handlers **Medium Severity** `_schedule_if_awaitable` fires async handlers with `ensure_future` and never waits for them. `close()` returns as soon as the message task finishes, so a `CLOSE` handler that suspends is still pending. `asyncio.run` then cancels leftover tasks, which drops that cleanup. Sync handlers used to finish inside `_emit_close` before `close()` returned.
Additional Locations (2) - [`src/elevenlabs/realtime/connection.py#L196-L201`](https://github.com/elevenlabs/elevenlabs-python/blob/02ffbfc5175a618dad6a4bfb67b951d35e252679/src/elevenlabs/realtime/connection.py#L196-L201) - [`src/elevenlabs/realtime/connection.py#L295-L304`](https://github.com/elevenlabs/elevenlabs-python/blob/02ffbfc5175a618dad6a4bfb67b951d35e252679/src/elevenlabs/realtime/connection.py#L295-L304)

## PR Summary

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
**Low Risk**
Scoped to realtime event dispatch; synchronous handlers behave as before, with clearer execution for previously broken async handlers.

**Overview**
**Fixes `async def` handlers on `RealtimeConnection.on(...)` so they actually run** instead of creating un-awaited coroutines.

`_emit` and `_emit_close` now detect when a handler returns an awaitable, schedule it with `asyncio.ensure_future`, and retain the task in `_handler_tasks` until it completes (so suspended handlers are not garbage-collected). Handler exceptions are still logged; sync handlers are unchanged.

Adds regression tests: async `OPEN`/`CLOSE` handlers run, and a suspended async handler completes after GC.
